deep.reconstruction:
Context (from the previous page): this is §§55–56 of the suppressed second part of Ramanujan's 'Highly composite numbers' paper. Here zeta_2(s) = 1 - 2^{-s} + 4^{-s} - 5^{-s} + ... = L(s, chi_{-3}). Qbar_2(N) is the coefficient of N^{-s} in zeta(s) zeta_2(s), so Qbar_2(N) = sum_{d|N} chi_{-3}(d). This equals r(N)/6 for the form x^2+xy+y^2. Qbar_2 vanishes unless every prime p = 2 mod 3 divides N to an even power. Otherwise Qbar_2(N) = prod over p = 1 mod 6 of (1 + a_p). pi_2 and theta_2 are the prime-counting and Chebyshev functions for primes p = 1 mod 6. The previous page shows that the extremal N have the shape N = exp(theta_2(x_1) + theta_2(x_2) + ...), with x_k = ((k+1)/k)^x. For these N, Qbar_2(N) = prod_k ((k+1)/k)^{pi_2(x_k)}.

(288) Without the prime number theorem: max order of Qbar_2(N) is 2^{(log N/loglog N)(1 + O(1/loglog N))}. [My gloss:] An upper bound comes from Qbar_2 <= d(N). A lower bound comes from N = product of primes = 1 mod 6 up to x, using only Chebyshev-type bounds theta_2(x) asymp x. Since x is about a constant times log N, log x = loglog N + O(1), and pi_2(x) = theta_2(x)/log x + O(x/log^2 x).

(289) Assuming the PNT for progressions with de la Vallée Poussin error, theta_2(x) = x/2 + O(x e^{-a sqrt(log x)}). Then log N = theta_2(x_1) + O(x_1^{0.585}) gives x_1 ~ 2 log N. Hence log_2 max Qbar_2 = pi_2(x_1) + ... = (1/2) Li(2 log N) + error. The x_2-terms are O(sqrt(log N)) and are absorbed.

§56 assumes RH for zeta and GRH for L(s, chi_{-3}).

(290) [My derivation:] From the explicit formulas, psi(x;6,1) = (psi(x) + psi(x,chi))/2. Also theta(x, chi) = psi(x, chi) - sqrt(x) + ..., since chi(p^2) = 1 for p != 3. Hence
  theta_2(t) - t/2 = -sqrt(t) - (1/2) sum t^rho/rho - (1/2) sum t^{rho_2}/rho_2 + O(t^{1/3}).
Next, pi_2(x) = theta_2(x)/log x + int theta_2(t)/(t log^2 t) dt. Expanding (1/2) Li(2 theta_2(x)) about x gives
  pi_2(x) - (1/2) Li(2 theta_2(x)) = int (theta_2(t) - t/2)/(t log^2 t) dt
  = -(1/log^2 x)(2 sqrt x + (1/2) sum x^rho/rho^2 + (1/2) sum x^{rho_2}/rho_2^2) + O(sqrt x/log^3 x).
So 2 pi_2 = Li(2 theta_2) - 2 R_2 + O(sqrt x/log^3 x), with denominators rho^2 and rho_2^2. The squares are needed for (292).

(291) S = sum 1/rho + sum 1/rho_2 = 1 + gamma + (1/2) log 3 + 3 log(Gamma(2/3)/Gamma(1/3)).
[My verification:] sum over zeta zeros gives 1 + gamma/2 - (1/2) log(4 pi). For the odd character chi_{-3}, Davenport's formula gives sum 1/rho_2 = L'/L(1,chi) + (1/2) log(3/pi) - gamma/2. The functional equation gives L'/L(1,chi) = gamma + log(2 pi/3) - L'/L(0,chi). Here L(0) = 1/3 and L'(0) = -(log 3)/3 + log Gamma(1/3) - log Gamma(2/3). Summing, all pi terms cancel and Ramanujan's closed form results exactly: S ≈ 0.07971 (zeta part 0.02310, L part 0.05662).

(292) Under RH, |rho|^2 = rho(1-rho). Hence sum 1/|rho|^2 = 2 sum 1/rho, and the same holds for rho_2. So |(1/2) sum x^rho/rho^2 + (1/2) sum x^{rho_2}/rho_2^2| <= S sqrt x. This gives (2 - S) sqrt x <= R_2(x) log^2 x <= (2 + S) sqrt x, which is exactly (292) since 3 + gamma + ... = 2 + S and 1 - gamma - ... = 2 - S.

(293) Numerically 2 + S = 2.0797 ≈ 2.080 and 2 - S = 1.9203 ≈ 1.920.

(294) [My derivation:] Write theta = log(3/2)/log 2, so x_2 = x_1^theta. log N = theta_2(x_1) + theta_2(x_2) + O(x_1^{0.415}) gives x_1 ≈ 2 log N and x_2 ≈ (2 log N)^theta = (3/2)(log N)^theta, using 2^theta = 3/2. Then
  log_2 Qbar_2 = pi_2(x_1) + theta pi_2(x_2) + ...
  = (1/2) Li(2 log N - 2 theta_2(x_2)) - R_2(x_1) + (theta/2) Li(x_2) + ...
  = (1/2) Li(2 log N) - (3/4)(log N)^theta/log(2 log N) + (theta/2) Li((3/2)(log N)^theta) - R_2(2 log N) + O(sqrt(log N)/(loglog N)^3).
This matches Ramanujan's phi(N) term by term, except that the argument of R_2 should be 2 log N.
errors: (290): R_2(x) is written with sum x^rho/rho and sum x^{rho_2}/rho_2. The correct explicit formula, and the bound (292) derived from it, need x^rho/rho^2 and x^{rho_2}/rho_2^2. With first powers the sums are not absolutely convergent and (292) would not follow. This is probably a slip of the pen (or my reading of the image).

(289): the error term O{log N e^{-a sqrt(log N)}} should be O{log N e^{-a sqrt(log log N)}}. The de la Vallée Poussin error applies at x ≈ 2 log N, so its exponent involves sqrt(log x) = sqrt(log log N). Compare Ramanujan's published d(N) result, 2^{Li(log N) + O(log N e^{-a sqrt(log log N)})}.

(294): the term -R_2(log N) should be -R_2(2 log N), because the largest prime used is x_1 ~ 2 log N (theta_2(x) ~ x/2). This mirrors the d(N) case, where x_1 ~ log N. The difference is of the same order as the main R_2 term, so it is not absorbed by the O-term.
(288): the claim 'without the PNT' is acceptable, but it still needs Chebyshev-type bounds for primes = 1 mod 6. That is elementary (or at least pre-PNT), but the page leaves it unstated.

results.what: Maximal order of Qbar_2(N) = sum_{d|N} chi_{-3}(d), i.e. r(N)/6 for x^2+xy+y^2: 2^{(log N/loglog N)(1+O(1/loglog N))} unconditionally, and 2^{(1/2)Li(2 log N) + error} under the PNT for progressions
results.modern_name: Maximal order of a multiplicative divisor-type function (representation numbers of a binary quadratic form)
results.usually_credited_to: Ramanujan (unpublished part of 'Highly composite numbers', published 1997 by J.-L. Nicolas and G. Robin)

results.what: Under RH+GRH: 2 pi_2(x) = Li(2 theta_2(x)) - 2R_2(x) + O(sqrt x/log^3 x), with R_2 built from 2 sqrt x and the zeros of zeta and L(s, chi_{-3})
results.modern_name: Explicit formula relating pi(x; q, a) and theta(x; q, a) under GRH (Ramanujan's Li(theta) device)
results.usually_credited_to: Ramanujan (1915 HCN paper for pi vs theta); explicit formulas from Riemann, von Mangoldt, Landau

results.what: Closed form sum 1/rho + sum 1/rho_2 = 1 + gamma + (1/2) log 3 + 3 log(Gamma(2/3)/Gamma(1/3)) ≈ 0.0797
results.modern_name: Sum over zeros 'B(chi)' constant: -Re B(chi) = sum Re(1/rho), for zeta and for L(s, chi_{-3})

results.what: Bounds (2 - S) sqrt x <= R_2(x) log^2 x <= (2 + S) sqrt x under RH, using |rho|^2 = rho(1 - rho)
results.modern_name: Standard RH bound on sum x^rho/rho^2

results.what: Second-order asymptotic (294) for the maximal order of Qbar_2(N) under GRH
results.modern_name: Refined maximal order under RH (analogue of Ramanujan/Robin results for d(N) and sigma(N))

deep.surprise_reason: This page belongs to the suppressed part of Ramanujan's 'Highly composite numbers', which was published and annotated by Nicolas and Robin in 1997, so its content is already attributed to him. The closed-form evaluation of the zero sum for zeta·L(s, chi_{-3}) is correct and neat but standard in principle. The remaining items are routine extensions of his d(N) analysis, with a couple of slips.
